title: Completing the augmented open projection square with its actual units
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site put $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and use the ordinary unbounded module derived category $D(B_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Open extension and restriction mean exact ringed-slice functors $e_!\dashv e^*$, applied termwise [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-open-immersion], $K\in D^b_c(U,R)$ and $P\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For $H\in D(B_W)$ write $H_n=H\otimes^L_{B_W}(A_n)_W$ and $Q_W(H)_\bullet=(\operatorname{Res}_n H_n)_n$, with the strict quotient transitions; $\operatorname{Res}_n$ forgets to $B_W$-modules along $B_W\to(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Use flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the total right derived inverse limit on strict towers, and its normalized Roos model and augmentation comparison [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit].
Let $H=j_!K\otimes^L_{B_X}P$, $H_U=K\otimes^L_{B_U}j^*P$, and $\gamma^B:H\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!H_U$ be the section-normalized ordinary open tensor map [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Let $T_\bullet,S_\bullet,\gamma_\bullet:T_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}JS_\bullet$ be the strict finite tensor towers and augmented map of [lem-sf-open-tensor-quotient-augmentation]; thus $T_n=\operatorname{Res}_n((j_!K)_n\otimes^L_{A_n}P_n)$ and $S_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}j^*P_n)$.
There is a specified natural isomorphism $\lambda_j:j_!R\lim S_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim JS_\bullet$: its Roos representative is the canonical product comparison on both signed mapping-fiber summands, and it carries the image of every strict augmentation to the corresponding strict augmentation [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Define
$$\Gamma_{K,P}=\lambda_j^{-1}\circ R\lim(\gamma_\bullet):j_!K\widehat\otimes^L_RP\longrightarrow j_!(K\widehat\otimes^L_Rj^*P),$$
using the recorded completed tensor functors [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. This is a natural isomorphism. With $\chi$ the actual quotient-augmentation tensor completion maps [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion], it satisfies the equality of actual morphisms
$$\Gamma_{K,P}\circ\chi_{j_!K,P}=j_!(\chi_{K,j^*P})\circ\gamma^B.$$
Both displayed $\chi$ maps are invertible, and under the canonical open units and completed tensor/restriction comparisons one has $j^*\Gamma_{K,P}=1$. In particular $\Gamma$ supplies the integral open projection datum of [def-exchange-projection], with its strict finite reductions and actual completion-unit normalization. The tensor/restriction comparisons here are those induced by restriction of the same augmented quotient systems and by the normalized exact-product limit map, including its units.

source.place: Tag 09BP, lemma-j-shriek-limits, applied to the ringed open extension via det-sf-open-closed-extension-zero-limits; Bhatt–Scholze Lemmas 6.5.5 and 6.5.8, pp.49–50. Agent-formulated augmentation-normalized Roos construction; old open-factor proof steps 8–9.

proof.text: First check the geometric hypotheses needed for the product and completion results. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: it has one point and its coordinate ring is a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $U$ and $X$ are Noetherian, hence quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] they are quasi-separated. Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is then quasi-separated: the preimage of an affine open $V\times_kV'$ of $X\times_kX$ under the diagonal is $V\cap V'$, quasi-compact because $X$ is quasi-separated, and such products cover $X\times_kX$. Apply [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] to $U\to X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: its composite is quasi-compact and its second arrow is quasi-separated. Thus $j$ is quasi-compact. Finally $\ell$ is invertible on both schemes because they are $k$-schemes and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. No separatedness of $X$ over $k$ is required.

source.place: Tag 09BP, lemma-j-shriek-limits; augmentation-normalized refinement of the open-factor paragraph of prop-sf-pf-coherence, using the cited strict Roos comparison.

proof.text: Use the exact additive ringed-slice extension $F=j_!$ of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Its canonical product comparison is invertible by [lem-cbc-ringed-open-extension-products], applied with $R=B_X$ and the quasi-compact open $j$. Countable products of modules over $B_U$ and $B_X$ are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Therefore [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] applies and defines $\lambda_j$ at $S_\bullet$. Its target is $R\lim JS_\bullet$: termwise $j_!$ of the $B_U$-module complexes $S_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(\cdots)$ is $\operatorname{Res}_n$ of the finite extension $j_!^{A_n}$, compatibly with all quotient transitions, because scalar restriction commutes with these open extensions by [lem-sf-open-tensor-quotient-augmentation]. In its signed model $\mathsf H(S)^q=(\prod_n S_n)^q\oplus(\prod_n S_n)^{q-1}$, the comparison is the product comparison $\phi$ on both summands. The equations with the product projections characterize this $\phi$; it commutes with $1-s$ and the differentials by naturality. The cited lemma supplies descent, naturality, invertibility, independence of resolutions, and preservation of every strict augmentation. This gives the specified $\lambda_j$, rather than just an unspecified isomorphism between limit objects.

source.place: Tag 09BP, lemma-j-shriek-limits; augmentation-normalized refinement of the open-factor paragraph of prop-sf-pf-coherence, using the cited strict Roos comparison.

proof.text: The finite tensor comparison $\gamma_\bullet:T_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}JS_\bullet$ of [lem-sf-open-tensor-quotient-augmentation] is an isomorphism of the simultaneous strict systems, not just a family of derived evaluations. Apply the total derived-limit functor to this isomorphism and compose with $\lambda_j^{-1}$. By [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], $R\lim T_\bullet=j_!K\widehat\otimes^L_RP$ and $R\lim S_\bullet=K\widehat\otimes^L_Rj^*P$, with the defining representative comparisons understood. This is exactly the displayed $\Gamma_{K,P}$; it is an isomorphism. Naturality follows by composing the natural transformations $R\lim(\gamma_\bullet)$ and $\lambda_j^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 09BP, lemma-j-shriek-limits; augmentation-normalized refinement of the open-factor paragraph of prop-sf-pf-coherence, using the cited strict Roos comparison.

proof.text:
Write $a_T:H\to R\lim T_\bullet$ and $a_S:H_U\to R\lim S_\bullet$ for the maps induced by the strict augmentations $c_T,c_S$. The augmented equality in [lem-sf-open-tensor-quotient-augmentation] is $\gamma_\bullet c_T=J(c_S)\Delta(\gamma^B)$. Apply the normalized Roos functor of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. On complexes the augmentation is $z\mapsto((c_n(z))_n,0)$, so the equality gives the same first coordinates and zero shifted coordinates on both sides. Thus it is an equality of the actual induced derived maps, not an inference from equal projections out of a homotopy limit. The augmentation assertion of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] identifies the map induced by $J(c_S)$ with $\lambda_j j_!(a_S)$. Consequently
$$R\lim(\gamma_\bullet)\,a_T=\lambda_j\,j_!(a_S)\,\gamma^B.$$
All uses of $R\lim$ here are on strict complexes of towers and their strictly commuting augmentation squares.

source.place: Tag 09BP, lemma-j-shriek-limits; augmentation-normalized refinement of the open-factor paragraph of prop-sf-pf-coherence, using the cited strict Roos comparison.

proof.text:
By [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion], the quotient augmentations defining $a_T,a_S$ are precisely those defining $\chi_{j_!K,P}$ and $\chi_{K,j^*P}$, respectively. The actual-unit convention of [def-sf-tensor-completion-comparison] uses the same first Roos coordinate and zero shifted coordinate. Thus $a_T=\chi_{j_!K,P}$ and $a_S=\chi_{K,j^*P}$ under the recorded tensor presentations. Multiplying the equality in the preceding step by $\lambda_j^{-1}$ gives the required equality
$$\Gamma_{K,P}\,\chi_{j_!K,P}=j_!(\chi_{K,j^*P})\,\gamma^B.$$
In particular this identifies the specified limit construction with the conjugate of the ordinary open map by the actual completion maps.

source.place: Tag 09BP, lemma-j-shriek-limits; augmentation-normalized refinement of the open-factor paragraph of prop-sf-pf-coherence, using the cited strict Roos comparison.

proof.text: The statement of [lem-sf-open-tensor-quotient-augmentation] gives both $j_!K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and $j^*P\in D^b_c(U,R)$. Together with the original assumptions on $K,P$, this allows [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion] to be applied to the pair $(j_!K,P)$ on $X$ and to $(K,j^*P)$ on $U$. The schemes are qcqs and $\ell$ is invertible by step 1. It follows that both displayed $\chi$ maps are isomorphisms. These applications require constructibility over the valuation ring $R$; they do not assume that the finite reductions have finite Tor dimension over the possibly nonregular rings $A_n$.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.5, pp.49-50; Lemma 6.5.8(2),(3), p.50; applied via the cited constructible tensor-completion and open-augmentation nodes.

proof.text: For restriction, use the localized site formula $j^*F(V/U)=F(V)$ of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and the sectionwise products of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]. Evaluating on $V/U$ identifies $j^*\prod_nF_n$ with $\prod_nj^*F_n$, with their actual projections. The same sectionwise limit formula identifies $j^*B_X=B_U$ from the quotient coefficient systems. Restriction is exact and additive by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Hence it too satisfies the hypotheses of the exact-product strict-limit comparison. Its comparison on a Roos complex is restriction of both signed coordinates. In particular it sends a quotient augmentation $z\mapsto((c_nz)_n,0)$ to its restricted quotient augmentation, so the tensor/restriction comparisons used here include the completion maps.

source.place: Tag 09BP, lemma-j-shriek-limits; augmentation-normalized refinement of the open-factor paragraph of prop-sf-pf-coherence, using the cited strict Roos comparison.

proof.text: Let $u:M\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*j_!M$ be the canonical open unit from [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], also for the strict system $S_\bullet$. That statement gives identity restriction for the simultaneous open tensor map; [lem-sf-open-tensor-quotient-augmentation] identifies $\gamma_\bullet$ with that finite tensor map with its quotient transitions. Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] to restriction as in step 7. The restricted product comparison defining $\lambda_j$ becomes the product of the units $u_{S_n}$: after each projection its equation is just naturality of $u$. This equality holds on both signed summands; therefore the restricted $\lambda_j$ identifies $j^*j_!R\lim S_\bullet$ with $R\lim j^*JS_\bullet$ through exactly the same $u$. Under $j^*T_\bullet\cong S_\bullet$ and $j^*JS_\bullet\cong S_\bullet$, the restricted $\gamma_\bullet$ is identity. Its Roos map is consequently identity on both products. Composing with the inverse restricted $\lambda_j$, and using $u_{R\lim S_\bullet}$, proves $j^*\Gamma_{K,P}=1$ under the stated completed tensor/restriction identifications. The augmentation calculation in step 7 shows that these are the comparisons with the actual units.

source.place: Tag 09BP, lemma-j-shriek-limits; augmentation-normalized refinement of the open-factor paragraph of prop-sf-pf-coherence, using the cited strict Roos comparison.

proof.text:
Finally compare with the integral open datum requested in [def-exchange-projection]. It asks for the natural open isomorphism together with its finite-reduction identifications and units. The preceding equality, and invertibility of the two $\chi$ maps, give
$$\Gamma_{K,P}=j_!(\chi_{K,j^*P})\,\gamma^B\,\chi_{j_!K,P}^{-1}.$$
Use these actual $\chi$ isomorphisms to identify each completed tensor with its ordinary tensor presentation. Under the strict coefficient-change and open-reduction comparisons of [lem-sf-open-tensor-quotient-augmentation], reduction of the resulting map is precisely $\gamma_n$ and the transitions are precisely those of $\gamma_\bullet$. This supplies the finite-reduction normalization, simultaneously for all $n$, with no choice of morphism lifts from their evaluations. The restriction normalization is step 8. Thus $\Gamma$ is the integral open projection datum on the stated constructible domain. This supplies the open tensor component of that definition, without asserting any of its separate proper, rational or algebraically closed coefficient existence claims.
